response.explanation: The new retry logic only increments retryCount when scheduleSMS returns falsy or throws. The enclosing `if (message?.length && message.length > 0 && sendTo)` has no else branch. A reminder with an empty message (no reminderBody and a non-REMINDER template) or no sendTo (e.g. a booking with no smsReminderNumber) is skipped without any increment. It stays scheduled=false and is re-fetched on every cron run, so the new retry cap never applies to it. Separately, the second OR branch of the deleteMany, `retryCount > 1`, has no `method: SMS` filter. Today only this SMS handler writes WorkflowReminder.retryCount, so other methods stay at 0. The unscoped clause would still delete email or WhatsApp reminders if they ever use the column. It would also delete SMS rows that are already scheduled=true, losing the referenceId needed to cancel the Twilio message.

response.consequence: A single failing or concurrently deleted reminder can stop the cron run before it schedules the remaining unscheduled SMS reminders. Those reminders are delayed until a later run and can be dropped if their scheduledDate passes first.
response.explanation: The new `prisma.workflowReminder.update` runs inside the `catch` block with no guard of its own. If that update throws, the error escapes the per-reminder `try/catch` and leaves `handler`. Two cases can trigger it. The reminder row may have been removed concurrently, for example by a cancellation, so Prisma raises a record-not-found error. The database may also be unavailable or may fail the write. The `for` loop then stops. Every later reminder in `unscheduledReminders` is skipped, and the cron request fails with a 500. Before this change the catch block only logged, so one bad reminder could not stop the others.
